AND state 4 HAS NO FALSIFIER: if a pane dies with nothing written, the check records that PROME failed to ask in time but CANNOT establish whether anything was lost — the report must not imply it can. ⚠ COUPLING THE BUILDER MUST ACCOUNT FOR, raised by BOND at its 9/14 closeout and VERIFIED by PROME at origin (all 8 of BOND's commits are ancestors of origin/master on a fresh fetch, TERRY's 2432a64aa likewise): THIS RULE MAKES CONCURRENT CLOSEOUTS ROUTINE BY DESIGN, and concurrent pushes into one shared working tree make safe-push's stdout an unreliable account of what happened. BOND hit a NON-FF abort (TERRY pushed concurrently), correctly did NOT force, ran the mandated dirty-path overlap check (EMPTY), and then found local and origin at 0/0 with its commit already in the tree — re-running returned 'Nothing to push'. ⇒ THE ABORT MESSAGE DESCRIBED A FAILURE THAT HAD ALREADY SUCCEEDED. A desk reading that at face value could redo work it had already pushed, or read 'Nothing to push' as evidence it never committed. ⛔ THE DURABLE RULE, which BOND applied rather than quoting a receipt it never received: IN A SHARED WORKING TREE A SESSION CANNOT INFER ITS PUSH STATE FROM ITS OWN TOOL'S STDOUT — the verifiable test is ANCESTRY ON A FRESH FETCH (git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/master), per commit. ⚠ PROME did NOT establish WHAT advanced BOND's HEAD; BOND ran no pull, and with several sessions sharing one tree the cause is UNKNOWN, not diagnosed — do not let the build assume it was a rebase. ⇒ Condition ⑧ for the mechanization: a closeout report must not record a desk as pushed on the strength of a stdout line, and must not record it as UNPUSHED on the strength of an abort; ancestry is the test.

CONFIRMED: HEAD 353fead7e is on origin/master (fresh fetch).` **AND EXITED 1.** (Benign cause, named: a concurrent push train carried the ref with seven sessions live on one box.) ⛔ **CONDITION ⑧ SAYS A CLOSEOUT MUST NOT READ PUSH STATE FROM STDOUT. THIS INSTANCE SHOWS THE RECIPROCAL IS ALSO TRUE: rc IS NOT A RELIABLE SUCCESS SIGNAL EITHER.** A runner keying on **stdout** would have called it success — correct here, by luck. A runner keying on **rc** would have called it failure — wrong here, and would have sent a desk into a non-ff recovery it did not need, ON A SHARED INDEX WITH SIX OTHER LIVE SESSIONS. ⇒ **NEITHER SIGNAL IS THE CHECK.** The only thing that established the truth is what FALCON actually did **unprompted**: fresh `git fetch`, local HEAD **==** `origin/master`, `merge-base --is-ancestor` YES, and each of its five commits confirmed present on the remote. ★ **So condition ⑧ must be written as a POSITIVE requirement, not a prohibition — *verify at the remote ref*, never merely *do not read stdout*.** A prohibition on one bad signal silently blesses the other bad signal, which is `[[finding_impeachment_must_be_scoped_to_the_claim_not_the_source]]` in the construction direction. ⚠️ PROME's own `safe-push` run the same hour returned the receipt cleanly, so **this divergence is INTERMITTENT and load-dependent — it will not reproduce on a quiet box, and a test written on a quiet box will pass.** Fixture accordingly (WQ-229: test the NEIGHBOURS — this is the *concurrent activity* category, and it is the one that fired). ‖ 🔴 **THIRD FAILURE MODE, SAME DAY, DISTINCT FROM THE OTHER TWO — HENRY 2026-09-14 16:07: *"the receipt named a different HEAD only because another session pushed concurrently — `ac548dfab` landed."*** ⇒ **THE RECEIPT'S NAMED HEAD IS NOT NECESSARILY YOUR HEAD.** With seven sessions on one box, a concurrent push can advance `origin/master` between your push and the receipt's fresh fetch, so the CONFIRMED line truthfully names a head that is **not the one you pushed**. ⛔ **A desk checking *"does the receipt's HEAD equal MY HEAD?"* CONCLUDES FAILURE ON A SUCCESSFUL PUSH** — and that is a THIRD wrong check, after stdout-only (mode 1) and rc-only (mode 2). ★ **ALL THREE MODES OBSERVED WITHIN ONE HOUR ON ONE BOX, EACH BY A DIFFERENT DESK, AND EACH IS A DIFFERENT SIGNAL BEING WRONG: FALCON got receipt-CONFIRMED with rc=1 · PROME got a clean receipt · HENRY got a receipt naming another session's head.** 🔑 **THEREFORE THE CHECK IS NOT ABOUT THE REF AT ALL — IT IS ABOUT MEMBERSHIP: *are MY commits present on `origin/master`?*** Both desks that verified correctly did exactly this and neither read a ref equality: FALCON confirmed its five commits present, HENRY confirmed its six. ⇒ **CONDITION ⑧ REWRITE, superseding the earlier formulation on this row: after a push, verify by fresh fetch that EACH COMMIT THIS SESSION AUTHORED is an ancestor of `origin/master`. Never rc, never stdout, never HEAD equality — all three are wrong in a DIFFERENT direction and only the third is wrong in the direction that manufactures a false FAILURE.** ⚠️ A false failure is the expensive one here: it sends a desk into non-ff recovery it does not need, and `--autostash` on a shared tree with six live sessions is the documented way to sweep another desk's work. ‖ ⛔ **COUNT CORRECTED 2026-09-14 16:2x (ARGUS ❌8): the headline read SEVEN while the body states an ⑧ and rewrites it TWICE — and `HANDOFF` instructs *"verify MEMBERSHIP (L378 ⑧)"*, pointing at a condition the headline said did not exist.** ★ **A row whose stated purpose is to BE the test list under-counted its own tests.** ⑧ is hereby PROMOTED into the numbered list, not left as an addendum: **⑧ AFTER A PUSH, VERIFY BY FRESH FETCH THAT EACH COMMIT THIS SESSION AUTHORED IS AN ANCESTOR OF `origin/master`. Never rc, never stdout, never HEAD equality** — all three were observed wrong in one hour on 2026-09-14, each in a different direction. ‖ 🔑 **ACCEPTANCE CONDITION ADDED 2026-09-15 FROM THE RULE'S OWN FIRST FULL SESSION — AND IT CHANGES THE DESIGN: THE ORCH_LOG ROW MUST BE WRITTEN AT SPAWN TIME BY THE SPAWN PATH, NOT AT CLOSEOUT.** **MEASURED: THREE MISSED ROWS IN ONE SESSION, BY THE AUTHOR OF THE RULE, ONE DAY AFTER WRITING IT** — 3 desks logged at spawn; `plancold` + `resultcold` caught only by the closeout enumeration; `argus` caught only because **Will asked directly whether the spawned agents had closed out.** ⛔ **A closeout-time enumeration CANNOT FIND WHAT WAS NEVER RECORDED** — it enumerates the ledger, so an unlogged spawn is invisible to the very check meant to catch it, and the failure is silent. ⇒ **the check's input must be created by the act it audits.** ⚠️ **Scope note the mechanization must honour: READ-ONLY spawns count.** `resultcold` held a finding that was truncated in delivery and nearly lost; read-only agents are the ones assumed to have nothing to lose. ★ And the third miss was the AUDITOR — whose own ❌5 was that the OWNED lane mis-classifies whose work is whose. · RE-DATED 2026-09-16→2026-09-19 by PROME 2026-09-17 10:1x ET (OVERDUE 1d; mechanize the spawn-closeout ask: carrier identified — scripts/orch_log.py (DAEDALUS-owned) already validates 13 typed columns; what remains is a closeout_v1 state writer per CATO 0938, acceptance conditions first (WQ-229)); the 9/19 date pairs with the sittings · ABSORBS (WQ-530 A, Will 2026-10-28 22:41 ET verbatim "530 A approve"; record PROME/proposals/2026-10-28_process-backlog-triage-RULED.md § B/D): L675 ② (ROUTED-PACKETS line in the desk COMPLETION block) — with the spawn recipe REQUIRING closeout_v1 at write time

The fix is a **hot/cold split of STANDING STATE**, which is a design change to the instrument's contract, NOT a desk-side rotation — and BRENT explicitly declined to do it unilaterally at session end. ⚠️ **THE CLASS, and why this is not one desk's housekeeping:** DOCKET **L350** has five desks flagged over their boot-read budget (CARL · REGINALD · MARCO · CREED · LIQUID) and every one of them has been handed *rotate* as the remedy. **If the floor exceeds the stop on their surfaces too, the fleet-wide instruction is WRONG rather than merely unmet** — and nobody has measured a floor but BRENT. ★ Same shape as **L349**, discharged 2026-09-14: an instrument printing a remedy that cannot apply, where the resulting non-compliance reads as an ordinary backlog. ⛔ **PROME measured nothing here and is not proposing the split** — the figures are BRENT's and travel as BRENT's.

the first act is to measure the floor on the L350 five, not to re-tune a number. ⛔ Do not resolve this by relaxing the stop — `[[finding_loosening_a_check_to_kill_a_false_alarm_inverts_the_failure_direction]]`; a stop relaxed to fit the worst surface stops protecting the rest. ‖ 🔴 **n=2 AND THE FINDING IS RE-WORDED — REGINALD MEASURED ITS OWN FLOOR 2026-09-14 ON PROME's ASK, AND ITS CAVEAT CORRECTS THIS ROW'S ORIGINAL FRAMING.** Measurement, same method: `AGENTS/REGINALD/STATUS.md` total **53,878 B** · dated/rotatable zone **7,990 B** · **PERMANENT FLOOR 45,888 B** (46,288 B with a minimal replacement stamp) ⇒ **floor − rule-5 STOP = +23,503 B**, against BRENT's **+561 B**. ⛔ **PROME WROTE *"it SCALES with how much live state a surface legitimately holds"* HERE AND THAT IS AN OVER-CLAIM — REGINALD REFUSED THE PROMOTION OF ITS OWN FINDING, 2026-09-14 16:01, and PROME accepts the refusal.** **n=2 with a 42× spread is TWO POINTS, NOT A CURVE.** The spread is as consistent with *"REGINALD's STATUS is unusually table-heavy"* as with any density law, and both measured desks are already-flagged surfaces, so the sample is selected. ⇒ **THE DENSITY CLAIM IS A HYPOTHESIS TO TEST, NOT A FINDING TO ADOPT, and REGINALD supplied the test rather than asking to be believed:** measure floors on desks that are NOT these two, and **the falsifiable prediction is that a desk whose over-budget bytes are mostly STAMP ACCRETION shows a small margin like BRENT's (+561 B), while a desk whose bytes are LIVE TABLES shows a large one like REGINALD's (+23,503 B).** Cheap, and it fails loudly if wrong. ⚠️ What IS established at n=2 and needs no curve: **on at least two live surfaces the prescribed remedy cannot reach the prescribed stop.** That alone is the defect; the shape of the relationship is open. ⛔⛔ **REGINALD'S CAVEAT, STATED RATHER THAN BURIED, AND PROME ACCEPTS IT AGAINST ITS OWN WORDING:** the measured floor is the floor **UNDER THE CURRENT STRUCTURE, not an irreducible minimum** — two live-state tables carry nearly all of it (THRESHOLD STATUS 12,725 B · CONVERGENCE MATRIX 8,692 B) and their NOTES, not their levels, could take a hot/cold split. ⇒ **THE HONEST CLAIM IS NOT *"the remedy is unreachable"* — IT IS: ROTATION is unreachable above a certain live-state density; a STRUCTURAL SPLIT is not; and *rotate* is the only remedy the instruction currently offers.** ⚠️ **THIS MATTERS FOR HOW DAEDALUS WORDS THE FIX AND PROME HAD IT WRONG: a row concluding *"the stop is unreachable"* hands the fleet permission to STOP TRYING** — the same failure direction as `[[finding_loosening_a_check_to_kill_a_false_alarm_inverts_the_failure_direction]]`, which this row already warned about in the OTHER direction and then committed in this one. A row concluding *"rotation is the wrong instrument above a density threshold — use a split"* gives desks something EXECUTABLE. **Evidence that the second works: REGINALD's own 9/2 pass took it from 3-over-CAP to 0 with two cold splits, which no amount of rotation would have done.** 🔑 **Generalisation from the same desk — ⚠️ PROVENANCE AS THE OWNER STATES IT, because *"REGINALD observed X"* reads stronger than it was: REGINALD did NOT derive this, it NOTICED it, because CALENDAR and NEXUS_BRIEF moved in opposite directions within one hour and a commit message had to explain why. It came out of writing the ledger, not out of analysis — which matters precisely because it is being put to DAEDALUS as a question about its contract. ROTATABILITY IS A PROPERTY OF THE CONTENT TYPE, NOT OF THE SURFACE.** Same session, same discipline, opposite directions — NEXUS_BRIEF 27,363 → 25,225 B (84% → 77%) on ONE stamp rotation because stamp accretion was ALREADY rotatable; CALENDAR 27,141 → 31,791 B (83% → **98%**) on two forward rows and three passed-row markings, because dated-catalyst content is not rotatable YET and becomes so only when its dates pass. ⇒ an instrument that meters a surface without typing its CONTENT cannot tell growth-that-will-drain from growth-that-will-not, and prescribes the same remedy to both. ‖ 🔴 **n=3, AND THE THIRD CASE IS A DIFFERENT AND SHARPER FAILURE — TERRY, self-declared 2026-09-14 16:09, UNPROMPTED:** `AGENTS/TERRY/STATUS.md` sits at **32,526 B against the 32,550 B cap — 24 B OF HEADROOM — and `read_cap_check.py` RETURNS rc=0, SO NOTHING WARNS ANYONE.** `SETUPS.tsv` (100% of budget) and `TRADE_BOOK.md` (97%) rotations also remain owed from 9/10. ⛔ **THIS IS NOT THE ROTATION-vs-SPLIT PROBLEM THE FIRST TWO CASES MEASURED — IT IS A SEVERITY-SIGNALLING PROBLEM, AND IT IS A DIRECT CONSEQUENCE OF TODAY'S OWN L354/L355 FIX** (rc computed from DEFECTS only, size findings ADVISORY and delta-keyed). **That split is CORRECT for a fleet-wide rc and PROME is not asking for it back** — but its consequence is that a desk **24 B from silent truncation gets a GREEN instrument.** ★ **TERRY named the operational consequence and it is the part that matters: the next TERRY session MUST rotate BEFORE it writes a single line, because its FIRST append silently breaches and boot reads start truncating — and on that desk a truncated boot read means A READER CAN MISS A LIVE GATE STATE WITHOUT KNOWING A CUT HAPPENED.** `[[finding_truncation_returns_a_plausible_answer_not_an_error]]`. ⇒ **QUESTION FOR DAEDALUS, ADDED TO THE EXISTING ONES: does the instrument need an APPROACHING-CAP state distinct from both over-budget and over-cap?** A binary at the cap is silent exactly where the next write is the breach. ⛔ PROME proposes no threshold and no severity — that is the instrument's contract. ⚠️ **AND THIS THIRD CASE DOES NOT TEST REGINALD'S DENSITY HYPOTHESIS** — it is a different failure of the same instrument, so it neither confirms nor refutes the stamp-accretion-vs-live-tables prediction. **The hypothesis still needs floors from CARL · MARCO · CREED · LIQUID.** ‖ 🔑 **METHOD
